summary.text: Full-stack software developer with four years of experience building and shipping production software.
Specialises in TypeScript, React/React Native and Node.js, with hands-on ownership across product development, backend architecture and AWS infrastructure.

Software Developer at ZIM Connections since October 2022, working on a production eSIM platform: a React Native app, white-label web platforms, a NestJS backend and the AWS infrastructure behind them.

Uses Claude Code daily across the development lifecycle while keeping ownership of scope, architecture and risk, and validates AI-assisted changes through automated tests, code review, CI and production monitoring.
Came to software through an economics degree and a six-month software engineering bootcamp in 2022, and is completing a software engineering degree apprenticeship alongside full-time work.

workingApproach.summary: The loop Alex runs on every piece of work, big or small. A failed pressure test goes back to Execute, and each delivery feeds the next round of scoping.

steps.title: Define the scope
steps.description: Write down what is in and, more importantly, what is out. Most project failures Alex has seen were scope failures wearing a technical costume.

steps.title: Evaluate the risk
steps.description: What breaks, who it hurts, what it costs, and what the rollback looks like. Decided before the first commit, not during the incident.

steps.title: Establish stakeholders
steps.description: Who signs off, who is affected, and who has to maintain it at 2am. Surfacing the quiet stakeholder early is worth a week of rework.

steps.title: Reuse before build
steps.description: In order: search the codebase for something that already does this, then look for a service that does it well and cheaply, and only then write something custom. Every line not written is a line that never has to be debugged, documented or migrated. Being lazy in the right direction is usually the best engineering decision available.

steps.title: Execute
steps.description: Build it. Claude helps here, treated as a very fast, very literal pair programmer that still needs someone with judgement holding the wheel.

steps.title: Pressure test
steps.description: Tests, edge cases, and honestly trying to break the work before a user does it for free.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.description: Shipped, monitored, documented. "It works on my machine" is a confession, not a status update.

steps.title: Communicate to the client
steps.description: In their language, not Alex's. Being able to explain a VPC to a non-technical stakeholder has been worth more to Alex's career than any single framework.

ai.text: Alex uses Claude daily and is open about it. AI sits in the Execute step of the loop, and earns its place there.
AI does not decide the scope, weigh the risk, or explain a design to a paying client. Alex sees those as the parts of the job that decide whether software is any good.
AI-assisted changes are validated through automated tests, code review, CI and production monitoring, and Alex keeps ownership of scope, architecture and risk.
At work, no secrets or customer data go into prompts, every line is reviewed, and nothing merges without passing the 2,600+ test CI gate.

Example: on ZIM@SBB, AI first-pass translations dropped two Italian keys and truncated a button on smaller iPhones. Alex caught both with a key-comparison script and on-device checks, and fixed them before release.
